scope: PR169 usage reads clear rejections: a foreground lane router on port 18797 with copies of the severus and personal logins and a planted weekly rejection on severus, run first with the installed router at the prior record and then with this code, against the real usage endpoint; real-account new/resume/restart checks; unchanged historical scenarios are references and were not rerun

matrix.scenario: severus token is outside the four-hour refresh lead
personal token is outside the four-hour refresh lead
Lane code and executable match the build at d4600fc
The installed router at the prior record keeps a planted weekly rejection after its start read shows the window below its limit
A start read that shows the weekly window below its limit clears the planted weekly rejection, and the account is ready
A start read at the weekly limit keeps the weekly rejection, while the five-hour and Fable windows read 0
severus is admissible with paid overflow disabled
new receives a routed 200 on the cleared account
Resume preserves account and conversation content
After restart, the cleared rejection stays cleared
Restart preserves the served conversation's account and content
Identity is the same at the start and the end
Live checks remain within the scoped request budget
Evidence contains no copied access token

incidents: The first restart attempt got 429 from the usage endpoint (retry-after 4m57s) on the fourth lane start read in 21 s for each account, so the lane refused dispatch and sent no inference. The daily router's next background read of the same two accounts also got 429 (retry-after 3m54s). Its readings stayed fresh, and its retry read succeeded at 2026-11-12T19:53:29-08:00. The restart step then ran once and passed.
The resume after restart came 5 min 11 s after the previous request, past the 5-minute prompt-cache lifetime, so it wrote the cache again on the same account (4,304 tokens) instead of reading it.

prior_acceptance.status: historical reference, not rerun at this code
